title: Lyric Genie Docs
text: Lyric Genie Docs What everything in the app is, where it lives, and how the pieces connect. Lyric Genie is a songwriter's notepad. You write lyrics, you capture ideas by voice, and the app keeps the two attached to each other so a hummed melody and the verse it belongs to never drift apart. Lyric Genie comes in two apps that share one account: the iOS app on iPhone and iPad, and the web app at app.lyricgenie.app. Use the iOS / Web switch in the top bar to pick yours. Where the two differ, the page says so, and the rest is the same for both. These docs are organised the way the app is: a page for each tab, a page for each kind of thing you make, and a page for every tool in the editor. Almost every question about Lyric Genie turns out to be a question about which thing something belongs to, which is why How it fits together is short and worth reading once. Your first song The short path, start to finish. How it fits together The five tabs, and what each one holds. The song editor Every control on the screen you write in. title: First launch
text: The first time you sign in, Lyric Genie asks you seven short questions before it lets you at the app. None of them takes longer than a tap, and two of them change how the app behaves afterwards. Step one of seven. The bar along the top is the whole wizard. The seven steps # Step What it asks What it does 1. Your name What should we call you? Becomes your display name , which is what co-writers see. Up to eighteen characters. 2. Role What best describes you? Songwriter, Artist, Producer or Hobbyist. Pick as many as fit. 3. Experience How much have you written? From Just Starting to Professional. 4. Where you found us How did you find us? Skippable, and the only step that is purely for us. 5. Voice Enable voice features The real iOS microphone and speech permissions. 6. Notifications Stay in the loop The real iOS notification permission. 7. In-line suggestions Enable In-line Suggestions A switch, on by default. The two that matter later # Voice. Microphone and speech recognition are system permissions, so this step hands you to iOS. Decline and Freestyle and recording cannot work at all. If you said no and changed your mind, it is in the iOS Settings app under Lyric Genie, not in Lyr

How it fits together
text: Lyric Genie has five tabs. Four of them hold a different kind of object, and the fifth is Settings. The web app has five places, which work the same way as the iOS tabs: Home , Songs , Concepts , Recordings and Settings . On a desktop, Songs, Concepts and Recordings run across the top bar, Home is the logo on the left, and Settings is in the menu under your avatar in the top right. In a narrow browser window all five become a bar along the bottom, as on iPhone. Four of them hold a different kind of object, and Settings is the fifth. Recordings
text: A recording is a piece of audio. You make one by recording in the app, or by importing a file you already have. Every recording either belongs to a song or does not yet. Both kinds appear in the Recordings tab, which is a list of all your audio regardless of where it came from. See The Recordings tab for that list and its controls. The two ways audio gets created # Recorded inside a song. Open a song, record, and the audio is attached to that song from the moment you stop. It also shows up in the Recordings tab. Recorded or imported on its own. Record from the Start tab, or import a file into the Recordings tab, and there is no song to attach it to yet. It sits in Recordings unattached. Recorded or imported on its own. Click Record or Import Audio at the top of the Recordings page, and there is no song to attach it to yet. It is saved as an unattached recording, which the web app calls an Idea. A record bar docks at the bottom of the page while you record. Recording from the Start tab. There is no song attached yet. Recording on the web needs Chrome, Edge or Safari. Firefox cannot record or import audio, because it cannot make the AAC audio Lyric Genie stores. See Supported formats

text: Freestyle records you and transcribes what you sang or said into editable lyrics. It is built for the moment where the melody arrives before the words do. title: Importing files
text: Lyric Genie imports two different kinds of file: audio, which becomes a recording , and text, which becomes lyrics. There are two routes in. Pick a file from inside the app, or send something to Lyric Genie from another app's share sheet. On the web you pick a file from your computer. There is no share sheet, so the iOS route of sending something from another app does not apply. Picking a file # Each kind has its own button. Import Lyrics sits beside the search field on the Songs page and takes text documents. Import Audio sits at the top of the Recordings page and takes audio files. Both open your browser's file picker. The import button in the top bar of the Start tab takes either kind. The app works out what it got by inspecting the file itself, not by trusting the extension, so a mislabelled file still lands in the right place. Audio goes to Recordings. Text goes to lyrics. If you already know what you are importing, the tab menus are explicit. Where Menu item Takes Songs tab ⋯ Import Lyrics from File Text documents Recordings tab ⋯ Import Audio from File Audio files These two were both labelled "Import from Files" in older versions, which made them impossible to tell

title: Genie chat
text: Genie is a chat that lives beside your song. Ask it about a line, tell it where you are stuck, or ask for a way into the next verse. It reads the song as it is right now, so you never have to paste your lyrics in. It is built to help you write your song, not to write it for you. Expect questions, options and short notes on what is working. Ask for a whole verse and it will write one, but it will not volunteer it. Sections and song structure
text: A section header is a line that names the part of the song underneath it. Lyric Genie picks them out, sets them in purple, and then uses them everywhere else. Naming your sections is optional, and it is the cheapest thing you can do to make the rest of the app work properly. Making one # Type the name of a section on its own line. That is the whole technique. Brackets are optional. The app strips them, so [Chorus] , (Chorus) , **Chorus** and plain Chorus all end up the same. Paste in lyrics from somewhere else and the headers usually survive the trip. title: Wish Workshop
text: Wish Workshop is the main AI writing tool. You open it with the genie lamp button at the bottom right of the song editor . title: Arrange mode
text: Arrange mode turns your lyrics into a checklist. Instead of a cursor and a keyboard you get a checkbox on every line, and a row of actions that move those lines around. It is for structure. title: Rhymes
text: Most rhyming dictionaries take one word and give you words that rhyme with it. Lyric Genie takes your phrase, works out which syllables carry the rhyme, and then looks for words and phrases that match both of them. That is the difference worth understanding before you use it. It is built for internal and multisyllabic rhyme, not just the word at the end of the line. Opening it # Select a line or a word, then tap Rhyme in the bar above the keyboard. See Selecting and editing lines . Select a line or a word and click Rhyme on the selection toolbar. The rhymes open in the Rhymes section of the right-hand panel, beside your lyrics, and a button in the section expands it to full height with every column side by side. On a phone browser it opens as a sheet, as in the app. With nothing selected, the panel offers rhymes for the last word of the line your cursor is on, and Insert puts the one you pick at your cursor. The sheet works on one line or less. title: The Master
text: Master is the version of the song you both agree on. It is not anybody's personal tab, and it is not whatever the last person typed. Lines get put there on purpose. Every shared song has one, at the end of the tab row, in yellow. 1 1 Always last in the row The bridge was sent first. Master still puts the chorus above it. You cannot type in Master # This is the thing to understand before anything else. Master is not editable. Tap the words and nothing happens: no cursor, no keyboard. There is no lamp button on this tab either, so no Wish Workshop and no in-line suggestions. The same holds on the web: the Master tab is read-only, and the Wish and Spark pill is not offered there. Everything in Master arrived from somebody's tab, and the only things you can do to it are reorder sections, delete them, or pull one back out. That is deliberate. If Master could be typed into, it would become a fourth draft competing with everyone else's, instead of the agreed version of the other three. To change a line, pull its section back to your own tab with Send to Me , edit it there, and send it again. (On the web, To Me on the selection toolbar does the same for the lines you have selected.) Waveforms # They show up on every device. Pro is bought in the iOS app. Free Pro Length of a single recording or import 5 minutes 60 minutes Total audio stored 60 minutes (1 hour) 10,000 minutes (about 167 hours) The per item cap applies to recording and to importing equally. A file you import cannot be longer than a recording you could have made. title: Supported formats
text: Audio # Format Extension Apple audio .m4a , .caf MP3 .mp3 WAV .wav AIFF .aiff , .aif AAC .aac , .mp4 FLAC .flac Everything is converted to M4A once it is in the app, on your device rather than on a server. On the web the conversion happens in your browser, and the file picker offers the same extensions. What actually opens depends on what your browser can decode, so MP3, WAV and M4A are the safe choices. After conversion a file must be under 60 MB, which a recording within your plan's length always is. Importing needs Chrome, Edge or Safari. Firefox cannot, because it cannot make the AAC audio that Lyric Genie stores. Recording on the web. A recording made in the browser is saved as an AAC .m4a (mono, 44.1 kHz), so it plays on your iPhone as well. Recording needs a browser that can encode AAC: Chrome, Edge or Safari. Firefox shows a message instead of recording. Detection is based on the file's actual type rather than its name, so a file with a misleading extension is still routed correctly. text: Lyric Genie names a few things in ways that are not obvious from the outside. This is what each one means. What you make # Song The document you write lyrics in. It holds the lyrics themselves, a title, an AI Context, a Scratchpad, any recordings you attach, and on a shared song a tab per writer. See Songs . Concept An idea that is not a song yet: a title, a mood, a theme, and optionally some similar artists. Concepts sit upstream of songs and can become one when you are ready. See Concepts . Recording A piece of audio. A recording belongs to a song, or to nothing yet. Either way it appears in the Recordings tab. See Recordings . Idea Web app only The web app's word for a recording that belongs to no song yet, which iOS labels Song Idea . Project A named, colour-tagged folder that holds a list of songs. The colour shows on the folder and above the title of every song in it. An album, an artist you write for, a session. See Projects . Inside a song # AI Context Three fields attached to the song: mood, theme, and similar artists. Everything the AI writes for that song is steered by them. title: FAQ
text: Answers here are deliberately short. Each one links to the page that goes into it properly. Is there a web version # Yes. The web app is at app.lyricgenie.app, and it runs in a desktop or phone browser. It covers writing, the rhyme and syllable tools, Wish Workshop, Genie, recordings, concepts, projects and collaboration. A few things are iOS only for now, including Freestyle, the share extension, the first-launch questions and account deletion. Each page of these docs says where the two differ, and the switch in the top bar picks which one you read. Do my songs sync between iPhone and web # Yes. Both apps use the same account, so a song written on one is there on the other, and lyrics, recordings, concepts and projects all appear in both. Sign in with the same Google or Apple button you use on your iPhone. See Signing in . Which browsers does the web app work in # Recording and importing audio need Chrome, Edge or Safari, because the browser has to be able to make AAC audio. Firefox cannot record or import audio. See Supported formats . Can I subscribe to Pro on the web # Not yet. Pro is bought in the iOS app, and the same plan then applies on the web. The web app shows your plan

Troubleshooting
text: Most of what looks like a bug in Lyric Genie is a control that is waiting for something. This page is grouped by where the problem shows up. Where did my work go # I signed in and my library is empty # You are almost certainly in the other account. Lyric Genie signs in with Google or with Apple, and those are two separate accounts even when both use the same email address. Songs written under one are invisible to the other. Sign out, sign back in with the other button, and check whether your songs are there. Nothing has been deleted. I recorded something and cannot find it in my song # Open the Recordings tab. If the recording was made from the Start tab rather than from inside a song, it is unattached and waiting there. Use Add to Song on it. This is the most common confusion in the app and it is worth reading How it fits together once to get the shape of it. My lyric sheet does not show the changes I made # A lyric sheet is a frozen snapshot , taken at the moment you created it. Editing the song afterwards never changes a link you have already sent, which is the point: what you sent a publisher last week still reads the way it did when you sent it. Make a new sheet when you want
